kurals.tr: Irandha Vekuliyin Theedhe Sirandha / Uvakai Makizhchchiyir Sorvu
kurals.m: More evil than excessive anger, is forgetfulness which springs from the intoxication of great joy

kurals.tr: Pochchaappuk Kollum Pukazhai Arivinai / Nichcha Nirappuk Kon Raangu
kurals.m: Forgetfulness will destroy fame, even as constant poverty destroys knowledge

kurals.tr: Pochchaappaark Killai Pukazhmai Adhuulakaththu / Eppaalnoo Lorkkum Thunivu
kurals.m: Thoughtlessness will never acquire fame; and this tenet is upheld by all treatises in the world

kurals.tr: Achcha Mutaiyaarkku Aranillai Aangillai / Pochchaap Putaiyaarkku Nanku
kurals.m: Just as the coward has no defence (by whatever fortifications ha may be surrounded), so the thoughtless has no good (whatever advantages he may possess)

kurals.tr: Munnurak Kaavaadhu Izhukkiyaan Thanpizhai / Pinnooru Irangi Vitum
kurals.m: The thoughtless man, who provides not against the calamities that may happen, will afterwards repent for his fault

kurals.tr: Izhukkaamai Yaarmaattum Endrum Vazhukkaamai / Vaayin Adhuvoppadhu Il
kurals.m: There is nothing comparable with the possession of unfailing thoughtfulness at all times; and towards all persons

kurals.tr: Ariyaendru Aakaadha Illaipoch Chaavaak / Karuviyaal Potrich Cheyin
kurals.m: There is nothing too difficult to be accomplished, if a man set about it carefully, with unflinching endeavour

kurals.tr: Pukazhndhavai Potrich Cheyalventum Seyyaadhu / Ikazhndhaarkku Ezhumaiyum Il
kurals.m: Let (a man) observe and do these things which have been praised (by the wise); if he neglects and fails to perform them, for him there will be no (happiness) throughout the seven births

kurals.tr: Ikazhchchiyin Kettaarai Ulluka Thaandham / Makizhchchiyin Maindhurum Pozhdhu
kurals.m: Let (a king) think of those who have been ruined by neglect, when his mind is elated with joy

kurals.tr: Ulliyadhu Eydhal Elidhuman Matrundhaan / Ulliyadhu Ullap Perin
kurals.m: It is easy for (one) to obtain whatever he may think of, if he can again think of it
